A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same forecasting research. All 14 pages of v1 and 12 pages of v3, including equations, tables, figures and references, support comparison. Neither supplied PDF contains an appendix.

before.justification: V1 reports original model-training experiments, forecasting accuracy and calibration measurements, failure analyses and hypothetical trading results.

after.justification: V3 reports original forecasting evaluations on a 1,265-question holdout, algorithm comparisons, failure analyses and hypothetical trading results.

M1.justification: The reported inference aggregation changes from averaging seven predictions in v1 Section 3.1 to median prediction sampling in the v3 abstract, although v3 provides little further explanation. The base model, rewards, GRPO/ReMax updates and guardrails remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions cover binary real-world forecasting using Polymarket questions and synthetic Foresight Learning training data. V3's filtered holdout changes sampling and evaluation procedures within this coverage; no additional task, domain or training-data source is established.

E2.justification: V3 Figure 2 adds standalone Lightning-100k ReMax to the trading comparison, alongside the ensemble and the four previously plotted methods. The accuracy-comparison membership remains unchanged. The trading prose still lists only four models despite the five plotted series.

E3.justification: The holdout changes from approximately 3,300 questions in v1, with 3,295 reported in Table 1, to 1,265 in v3. Section 2.1 adds scheduled-close eligibility, o3 screening for leaked news information and exclusion of zero-volume questions throughout evaluation. Brier/ECE definitions, one-cent trading costs and all three bet-selection rules are retained.

E4.justification: V3 adds a single-versus-ensemble ReMax trading comparison and replaces the confidence-dependent GAM and break-even analysis with binned market-probability estimates. The separate per-trade return analysis disappears. Guardrail failure cases and accuracy comparisons across training scale and ensembling remain.

E5.justification: V3 retains Wald Brier intervals, bootstrap ECE intervals and pairwise significance stars, but removes reporting of the 9,999-replicate paired profit bootstrap, per-trade Welch tests and bootstrapped break-even interval. Trading ROI comparisons consequently have substantially less uncertainty reporting, although Figure 3 still supplies error bars and a subgroup interval.

E6.justification: Results are extensively replaced on the revised holdout. Table 1 changes ReMax ensemble Brier/ECE from 0.193/0.0424 to 0.190/0.062; Modified-GRPO now has lower ECE than the ensemble. V3 reports all-market profits of $52 for the ensemble, $54 for Modified-GRPO and $39 for o1, and adds standalone ReMax trading results. These are different-holdout results, not demonstrated same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: The Brier reward definition, GRPO objective, modified advantage and ReMax objective are unchanged. Neither version adds formal propositions or proofs; revisions to empirical statistical analyses do not establish a theoretical change.

C1.justification: V1's central accuracy claim is statistical parity with o1; v3's results and conclusion claim significant superiority, supported by its revised Table 1, although the introduction still says 'same accuracy.' V3 also foregrounds a novel evaluation dataset and approximately 10% all-market ROI, replacing the emphasis on a significant high-edge profit advantage.

C2.justification: V3 replaces v1's assertion of fully eliminating look-ahead bias with specific leakage risks and measures intended to minimize them. It explicitly interprets trading as testing information beyond market prices despite inferior Brier scores, while dropping v1's proposed information-lag explanation for poor performance against confident markets.

D1.justification: V3 identifies o3 as the leakage-screening tool and documents additional test exclusions; optimization and hardware details remain. Its conclusion now specifies 10k real plus 90k synthetic questions, conflicting with Section 2.1's retained 10k plus 100k description. This is a documentation inconsistency, not reliable evidence of a changed training budget.

R1.justification: V3 adds Paleka et al. (2025), 'Pitfalls in evaluating language model forecasters,' to motivate temporal-leakage precautions. The remaining cited works and positioning relative to GRPO, Dr. GRPO, ReMax and DPO are retained.

P1.justification: The abstract, substantial introduction passages, data section, results narrative and conclusion are rewritten. The separate main-model accuracy subsection is merged into the algorithm comparison, and the detailed trading subsections are condensed into a shorter narrative.

P2.justification: V3 changes the title/author arrangement, heading typography and running rules throughout, and places the introduction on the first page. Table 1 is reordered, Figure 2 gains a series, and Figure 3 replaces the smooth curve and confidence band with five bins and error bars over a different horizontal range.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1's broad assurance that chronological separation eliminates look-ahead bias, v3 documents concrete safeguards against resolved-question selection bias and misdated news, strengthening evaluation credibility. The gain is limited by substantially reduced profit uncertainty reporting and unresolved inconsistencies in training counts and trading-comparator descriptions.
